scenes.title: Proof on the Point at Issue
scenes.summary: Proofs should be demonstrative and aimed at the point disputed, whether the fact, the harm, its extent or its justice; only when the fact is disputed must one side be wicked. In epideictic, amplification shows that deeds are noble and beneficial; in deliberative speech one disputes whether a thing will happen or is just; a lie outside the subject is a tekmērion of others.

scenes.title: Examples, Enthymemes and Maxims
scenes.summary: Examples suit speaking to the assembly, enthymemes the courts. Enthymemes should be mixed in, not strung in a row, and limited in number, “as much as a sensible man would” say; they should be kept out of passages of emotion and character, for demonstration has neither character nor choice. Maxims serve both narration and proof.

scenes.title: Advice Is Harder
scenes.summary: Speaking to the assembly is harder than pleading in court, for it concerns the future, while even seers know the past, as Epimenides the Cretan said, and the courts have the law as a starting point. When at a loss, the adviser should accuse, as Isocrates does; epideictic speeches should be varied with episodes of praise, as Gorgias never ran short of things to say.

scenes.title: Character, Refutation and Order
scenes.summary: Without demonstrations, speak so as to show character, which suits a decent man better. Refutative enthymemes are better liked than demonstrative ones. The first speaker states his proofs and then meets the other side, unless its arguments are many, as Callistratus did in the Messenian assembly; the second speaker first demolishes his opponent's speech, as Hecuba begins with the goddesses.

scenes.title: Character Through Others
scenes.summary: Since speaking about oneself invites envy and about others abuse, put the words in another's mouth, as Isocrates does in the Philippus and the Antidosis, and Archilochus with the father of the bride and with Charon the carpenter, and Sophocles with Haemon. Enthymemes may also be turned into maxims.
